3 · What the numbers say

Power Systems is the biggest block (≈ 12 questions). The Tamil Nadu papers asked 137 power-system questions — and a large share was renewable energy: solar radiation (13), wind turbines & Betz limit (17), fuel cells (8), solar PV (6). Tamil Nadu is one of India's largest wind and solar states, and TNEB is a power utility, so generation, renewables, protection and per-unit faults are safe bets.

Circuits & Fields (≈ 11) — Thevenin, maximum power, resonance, ac power, power-factor correction, 3-phase power and Gauss's law are asked in almost every paper.

Control Systems (≈ 8) — TANGEDCO 2018 had 12 control questions (its largest unit). Routh–Hurwitz came in 9 state papers (and 11 GATE years); Mason's gain, steady-state error, state space and 2nd-order specs repeat.

Electrical Machines (≈ 8) — the synchronous motor (V-curves, excitation) is the single most repeated machine concept (12 state questions); also transformer emf/efficiency, dc motor back emf, induction slip and starters.

Digital & Microprocessors (≈ 6) — 8085 basics came 12 times in the TNPSC papers; Boolean algebra, counters, logic families and the 8051 complete the unit.

Power Electronics (≈ 5) — SCR basics, choppers, phase-controlled converters, inverters and IGBT.

Networks / computer control (≈ 1) — one OSI/data-link question is typical.

6 · Strategy for −⅓ negative marking

A pure guess among 4 options: expected mark = ¼ × 1 − ¾ × ⅓ = 0. Guessing blind neither helps nor hurts on average.

If you can rule out one option: ⅓ − ⅔ × ⅓ = +1/9 per question → attempt.

If you can rule out two options: ½ − ½ × ⅓ = +⅓ per question → always attempt.

Time: 120 minutes for 100 questions = 72 s each. Do Part III first (60 marks), then Part I, then Part II; leave lengthy numericals for the second pass.

Target: attempt 85+, accuracy 85 % → about 70 marks after negatives.

7 · If you have only one week — revise these first

1. Renewables: solar constant & PV cell, wind power ∝ V³ and Betz 59.3 %, fuel cells.

2. Synchronous motor V-curves and excitation; induction motor slip, Ns, star–delta.

3. Routh–Hurwitz, Mason's gain, steady-state error, 2nd-order specs.

4. Thevenin/maximum power, resonance, ac power & pf correction, 3-phase star/delta.

5. Per-unit change of base, fault types, Buchholz/differential/distance relays, Ferranti effect, SIL.

6. 8085 basics & instructions, 8051 features, Boolean algebra, counters, logic families.

7. Measurement errors, instrument types (PMMC/MI), CT/PT, bridges.

8. AM/FM/PCM formulas; sampling, DFT/FFT counts.
